Writ Petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, has been filed by the Petitioner seeking withdrawal of the Look Out Circular ('LOC') opened against him by the Respondent.
2.

The Petitioner has stated that he was in Mumbai, to attend the marriage anniversary of a professional acquaintance, when he was brought back to Delhi by Income Tax department and a search and seizure operation was carried out at his residence and office between 30.06.2019 and 05.07.2019.

3. Summons were issued by the Income Tax Department directing the Petitioner to be present for his personal deposition on 17.07.2019, 02.08.2019 and 09.12.2019 under Section 131(1A), for his personal deposition.
4. The Petitioner duly responded to the summons as were received by This is a digitally signed order.

The Petitioner joined the inquiry on two occasions i.e., on 09.08.2019 and 30.12.2019 and answered all the questions as were put to him by the officers of the IT Department.

He also submitted a written Amarendra Dhari Singh vs Central Bureau Of Investigation on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164403208/
1 explanation about the documents and data as were seized during the search operation conducted, as directed by the summons dated 09.12.2019.

sentences.text: 5. The Petitioner has given a detailed history of medical ailments.

He has submitted that he was first diagnosed with lymphatic cancer in 2001 and was regularly undergoing a highly specialised treatment under the supervision of Dr. Morton Coleman at the Centre for Lymphoma & Myeloma,
Weill Cornell Medicine/ New York Presbyterian Hospital in 2001-2002.

sentences.text:
Despite all the precautions,
the Cancer recurred on three previous occasions, i.e. in 2004, 2013 & 2015.
6. Further, in 2011, the Petitioner was diagnosed with hyperthyroidism of the eye glands, which has caused excessive bulging and frequent uncontrolled tearing of the eyes.
The Petitioner has been in regular treatment for the same as well.

7. In January, 2016 on being examined by Dr. Richard S. Haber, MD, Profession of Medicine,
Endocrinology at the Icahn School of Medicine, Mount Sinai, New York, USA, the Petitioner was advised Thyroid Function Test every six months to monitor the relapse of hyperthyroidism, or possible future hypothyroidism.

sentences.text: He was also advised ophthalmologic observation to detect any worsening of orbitopathy or loss of vision in the eye.
8. In the end of 2019-early 2020, the Petitioner had a recurrence of the symptoms of the Cancer such as sudden bouts of sweating and severe itching.
He also received e-mails dated 02.09.2019 and 25.12.2019 from Dr.

It was thus,
imperative that he undergo the Tests at the earliest.

9. On 09.08.2019, the Petitioner informed the concerned officer of the Income Tax Department regarding his deteriorating medical condition and immediate need to travel to America for a check-up, and follow up tests.
He was informed about the opening of LOC against him by the Income Tax Department.
Around the same time, during the course of the FEMA inquiry being conducted by the ED, the Petitioner learned that the ED had also opened a LOC against him.

10. In view of the same, the Petitioner addressed representations to both the Agencies, requesting them to permit him to travel abroad and consequently withdraw the respective LOC's opened by them against him.
However, it was all to no avail.

11. Thereafter, the Petitioner approached this Court vide Writ Petition (Civil) No. 147/2020 titled Amarandra Dhari Singh v. Income Tax Department & Anr. seeking quashing of both the LOCs opened against him.

The ED informed this Court that they have only opened an intimation LOC against the Petitioner, which was recorded in Order dated 03.02.2021.
The Petitioner has also cooperated with the ongoing inquiry being conducted by the ED.

13. The Petitioner had last travelled to New York, USA for his check-up on account of the recurrence of the symptoms of the lymphatic cancer in February 2020, his PET/CT scan revealed several small to mildly enlarged lymph nodes in the neck, chest and abdominal regions.
He was advised to travel for follow up tests in September-October, 2020.
However, he was unable to travel due to the Covid19 Pandemic and the travel restrictions announced by the American Government.
14. The Petitioner was thereafter, scheduled to travel to America in May 2021.
However, the American President issued Proclamation dated 30.04.2021 suspending the entry of non-immigrants from India to America with effect from 04.05.2021.

It is submitted that on account of the gravity of the Petitioner's medical condition, he reached out to the Ministry of External Affairs telephonically and vide email dated 10.05.2021 sought special permission to travel to the USA.

15. Upon being directed by the Ministry, he addressed his request to the American Embassy at New Delhi vide email dated 17.05.2021 seeking permission to travel to America, accompanied by his sister, Mrs. Priya Sinha and her husband.

The Petitioner was granted special permission from the American Embassy, New Delhi to travel to New York, America for emergency medical treatment between 25.05.2021 to 24.06.2021.
16.
During this period, the Respondent registered FIR against the Petitioner for the alleged commission of offences punishable under Section This is a digitally signed order.

Pursuant to the registration of FIR, a search/ raid was conducted at his residence and office premises on 19.05.2021, in which he and his employees duly cooperated.
17. It is submitted that no summons has been issued since then regarding the said LOC.

However,
the Petitioner has assured the Respondent of his continued cooperation with the ongoing investigation.

sentences.text: Vide Letter dated 24.05.2021, the Petitioner had addressed to the Respondent in order to inform regarding his impending travel and the gravity and urgency of the situation.
He requested the Respondent to intimate the concerned Immigration Authorities/FRRO to permit the Petitioner to travel on the dates, as would be intimated by the Petitioner to the Respondent.

On account of the short window to travel, the Petitioner followed up with the concerned officer of the Respondent the next day i.e. on 25.05.2021 enquiring regarding the status of his representation and whether a LOC had been opened against him.
He was informed that the Respondent had opened a LOC against him and that his representation would be processed at the Director General level and take at least one week.
The details of LOC were not provided to him.
19. The Petitioner is seeking the withdrawal of the LOC on the ground of his deteriorating health.

The New York Presbyterian Hospital possesses the necessary infrastructure as well as a team of highly skilled Oncologists advised by Dr. Morton Coleman, who is known globally for his treatment of lymphoma, myeloma, leukaemia and Hodgkin's lymphoma and various accolades.
Dr. Morton Coleman has been treating the Petitioner for the last two decades, since the detection of the lymphatic cancer for the first time in This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

Accordingly, he is aware of all the complications which have arisen on the past four occasions when the Petitioner was diagnosed with the Cancer and which have resurfaced on account of the delay in the treatment.
20. The Petitioner's medical condition is genuine, serious and grave.
He has been compelled to undergo regular treatment and Pet Scans and Bone Marrow Tests for the early detection and containment of the disease.
However, even upon taking all the necessary precautionary tests and treatment, the disease relapsed on four occasions.

Further, as per the advice of Dr. Coleman, in his emails dated 14.05.2021 and 19.05.2021 in case the malignant cancer is left untreated for a long duration, it would be more difficult to treat in the future.
21. The Petitioner is 62 years old.
He also suffers from high blood pressure, hypertension, diabetes and thyroid for which he takes routine medicines.
All the ailments cumulatively are further aggravating the Petitioner's health.

Therefore, it is crucial for the Petitioner to get treated from the same doctor who is acquainted with his ailment and the various complications that may arise, as have arisen in the past.
22.
The Petitioner's decision to travel for his much-delayed treatment of lymphatic cancer, was planned much prior to the registration of the FIR.

Furthermore, the first medical certificate from Dr.
Coleman pertaining to his condition and illness, was issued on 14.05.2021, i.e. three days prior to the registration of the FIR.
Therefore, under no circumstance, is it the intention of the Petitioner to flee from the country.
He is required to travel on priority to get the appropriate medical attention on account of his ill health.

The Petitioner does not have any pending bank loan or demand from any government agency against him.

Furthermore, there is no other complaint against the Petitioner,
which would justify the issuance of the LOC by the Respondent.
24. The Petitioner has sizeable moveable and immovable assets in India and is a regular Income Tax payee.
His annual income is computed in the highest tax slab.
In the last three financial years, the Petitioner paid a cumulative personal tax of Rs. 9,52,37,781/-.
The Petitioner is also cooperating in the inquiry being conducted by the IT Department and the ED.

25. As per the mandate of Article 21 of the Constitution of India, a person cannot be deprived of his personal liberty or life without complying with a fair, just and reasonable procedure, in accordance with law.
Such procedure cannot be fanciful or oppressive.

Furthermore, the due application of mind by the authority to the relevant factors that would enable opening of LOC/impounding of a passport, must be evident and duly exercising by the issuing authority.

26. It is submitted that an ongoing investigation or inquiry being undertaken by an investigating authority, cannot be an embargo and treated as a condition for curtailing the personal liberty of an individual to travel abroad, especially in emergent situations.
It would amount to a grave miscarriage of justice.

27. Reliance has been placed by the Petitioner on the judgement of this Court in Sumer Singh Salkan vs. Assistant Director & Ors. ILR (2010) VI Delhi 706 wherein it was held that the purpose of opening a LOC against an individual is to secure the presence of that individual during investigation or

28. The Respondent does not have any cogent reason to resort to the coercive measure of opening of LOC against the Petitioner.
29. The Petitioner hence, prays for a direction to the Respondent to withdraw the LOC issued against the Petitioner.
30. A Status Report has been filed on behalf of the CBI wherein they had objected to quashing of the LOC.
Submissions Heard and Record and the Judgments, perused.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The circumstances in which the Look Out Notice can be opened has been explained in the decision of this Court in Sumer Singh Salkan (Supra) decided on 11.08.2010.

It was observed that "Recourse to LOC can be taken by investigating agency in cognizable offences under IPC or other penal Laws, where the accused was deliberately evading arrest or not appearing in the trial court despite NBWs and other coercive measures and there was likelihood of the accused leaving the country to evade trial/arrest".
32.
In the present case, none of the circumstances are made out.

It is evident that the Petitioner has been duly cooperating with the Investigating Agencies in the search and seizure proceedings, and has been making himself available whenever the summons were issued.
33. Further, the Petitioner has explained that his family, property, employment and residence is in India.

However, owing to requiring treatment for his medical conditions and for business reasons,
he has to travel abroad and he had previously been permitted to travel on several occasions previously.
The conduct of the Petitioner reflects that there is no likelihood of his leaving the country, to evade trial.
34. Given these facts, that petitioner has joined investigations; is not This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 21/11/2025 at 21:37:21 evading the process of law and there is no likelihood of the petitioner leaving the country to evade trial; none of the grounds as stated in Sumer Singh Salkan (Supra) for continuing the LOC, continue to exist.
The Lookout Circular (LOC) issued against the Petitioner is hereby, quashed.
35. The Petitioner shall keep the Trial Court informed about his place of residence and his updated contact details.
In the event of travelling abroad, he may inform the Trial Court by way of an Application with his itinerary annexed and details of the intended placed of residence abroad.
36. The Writ Petition is allowed, in the aforesaid terms.
Pending Application(s), if any, stand disposed of.
NEENA BANSAL KRISHNA, J NOVEMBER 7, 2025
